newsitem.title: INDIA: India Essar targets 25 bln rupee sales.
newsitem.headline: India Essar targets 25 bln rupee sales.

text.p: Indian steel maker Essar Steel Ltd said it expected sales for the financial year ending on March 31, 1997, to cross 25 billion rupees.

"With the increase in the international price of steel, and higher sales volume in the second half of the year, the company expects to have a much better second half in terms of sales and net profits," it said in a statement after a board meeting.
Sales in the first six months ended September 30, 1996, amounted to 9.37 billion rupees.

Essar said the commencement of commercial production on April 1, 1996, leading to a higher depreciation charge of 1.21 billion rupees (against 221 million in the year ago period) and net interest of 1.71 billion rupees (against 0.6 million) and a weak steel market led to the firm posting a net loss of 476 million rupees for the six months ended September 30, 1996.

It said Essar's two million tonnes a year integrated steel plant in western India was now fully stabilised. It produced 633,000 tonnes and sold 582,000 tonnes of steel in the first six months of 1996/97 (April-March). The company expected to produce about 1.4 million tonnes for the full year.
The hot briquetted iron (HBI) plant produced 706,000 tonnes during the first six months. Essar expected to produce 1.5 million tonnes of HBI by the year-end.
Essar said it exported over 100,000 tonnes of hot rolled coils and 69,000 tonnes of HBI to Europe, Japan, Middle East and Far East valued at 1.57 billion rupees in these six months.
"Likely exports during the year are expected to be 200,000 tonnes of hot rolled coils and 150,000 tonnes of HBI.
Essar said a new 3.3 million tonnes a year iron ore pelletisation plant in the south-eastern port city of Visakhapatnam had started trial production.
"The company would now not require to import high quality pellets from international suppliers," it said.
Essar's joint venture in Indonesia, P.T. Essar Dhananjaya, also started trial production during the first half of 1996/97.
"This would open the market for exports of upto 150,000 tonnes of hot rolled coils annually to Indonesia, giving further impetus to the company's export activities," Essar said.

"The company now believes that the bottom for the steel prices has been touched and an upward trend has already begun. This is reflected in international prices of hot rolled coils increasing to $320 to $330 per tonne currently," it said.
Prices touched a low of $290 per tonne in the last one year, "much below the bottom of the normal steel cycle," it said.
"Even in the first year of commercial operations, the company will be in a position to meet all its interest and debt commitments and have a positive contribution," it forecast.
